reason: Measured in Playwright at 390x844, every number in the finding is exact and the pairs compared are the right ones. Both states resolve to the same medium (data-medium=phone for state=loading and state=phone), so this is not a medium mismatch. state=loading: .b-who y=264, first skeleton slab (107x86, the stand-in for the count) y=301, .b-todayLabel y=516, .tl-stage y=236, page height 844. state=phone: .b-who y=28, .b-count y=65 (86 tall, the same 86px the slab reserves), .b-todayLabel y=280, .tl-stage y=0, page height 1692. Delta is exactly +236 on all three, and the internal proportions match to the pixel (who-to-count +37 both, who-to-rule +252 both), so the entire block is translated, not deformed. Cause is master.html:268 - [data-state="loading"] .tl-page { justify-content: safe center; min-height: 100dvh; }. The page does not scroll (scrollHeight 844 = viewport), so on arrival the name and count the guest is already reading jump 236px up, 28% of the screen. Not covered by the gates: interaction-check.mjs:1768 ("nothing hops when the data lands") measures .b-todayLabel MINUS .b-who and its own comment concedes it does so because "an absolute comparison would be measuring the centring rather than the hop" - i.e. the translation was seen and excluded from measurement, not designed correct. interaction-check.mjs:2116 asserts loading centres in its room only at 1440x960; :652 asserts only top >= -1 at 390, which a top-aligned frame passes. Not settled: the round-9 SETTLED list covers the skeleton's FILLED SLABS, not its position, and the lessons-library entry ("sized to their real geometry") is about size only. Two further facts make it worse rather than defensible. First, the sibling face already ships the fix: state=loading-slow is not matched by the [data-state="loading"] selector, so its .b-who renders at y=28, byte-identical to the arrived plan - the two loading faces are 236px apart at 390 while render-b.js comments that "nothing moves between the two faces". Second, round 8 already applied exactly this correction elsewhere ("The empty project stands on the page's own margin"). Simulated the proposed fix by injecting justify-content: flex-start under a max-width:1023 query: .b-who lands at 28, the slab at 65, the rule and "Today is 16 July" at 280 - a pixel-exact tracing of what replaces it, with the arrival changing only slabs into words. No constraint touched: no colour, no weight, no architecture.
sharpenedFix: Scope the centre-in-the-room rule at master.html:268 so it stops applying to loading below the two-column breakpoint - leave publish, day, ended and unfurl centred, and let the loading .tl-page sit on justify-content: flex-start so .b-who renders at the y it keeps (verified: 28, matching state=phone and the already-top-aligned loading-slow).
